where: Section 3, Figure caption and figure aria
problem: Section 3 correctly says Carson sits above 2Δf by 2f_m, and the caption correctly says the gap is 2f_m = 30 kHz. But the same paragraph then says the two estimates 'meet only as β grows', the caption says 'the two estimates meet only for large β', and the aria says 'the two curves merge once β is large'. The two curves never meet: Carson = 2Δf + 2f_m, so the separation stays exactly 30 kHz at every β. Only the relative gap (30 kHz divided by 2Δf) shrinks. A student will read 'meet' as the curves converging to one value, which contradicts both the formula and the plotted points.
fix: Replace with: 'The figure plots both estimates for f_m = 15 kHz. They stay 2f_m = 30 kHz apart at every β; only the relative gap 2f_m/(2Δf) = 1/β shrinks as β grows, so 2Δf becomes a good approximation for large β.' Change caption ending to 'the two estimates remain 30 kHz apart; the relative gap shrinks as β grows', and change the aria to 'For a 15 kHz tone the Carson estimate stays 30 kHz above 2Δf; the relative gap shrinks as β grows.'

problem: 'The total power stays A_c²/2 because the Bessel squares sum to 1' gives a power value in V² with no resistance stated. A_c²/2 is the power only when the wave is delivered to a 1 Ω resistance; students often quote A_c²/2 as watts without knowing why.
fix: Write: 'The total power stays A_c²/2 (in W, across a 1 Ω resistor) because Σ J_n²(β) = 1, so the sidebands simply take power from the carrier.'
